topics: Benchmark plan: 24h staging run + KV cache behavior
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood CSM), Jenna (CTO - Starlit Tech), Omar (Platform), Priya (SecOps), Elliot (PM)

Summary: Quick intro, dive on infra constraints, security checklist, agree sprint plan for staging benchmarks and next steps.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. super quick intros around the room?
[00:12] Jenna (CTO): Jenna, CTO here at Starlit, we're moving our chat+search feature to live in Q4 and want to validate latency and cost.
[00:20] Omar (Platform): Omar, platform eng. running mainly on GCP, want to understand network egress, VPC peering, and whether we need any on-prem pieces.
[00:28] Maya: Great. Carlos is our SE, he'll drive the technical bench. Carlos?
[00:34] Carlos (SE): hi all. quick note: we'll propose two paths — Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) or Redwood Private (VPC/private control plane). We'll run staged benchmarks to show expected p99 latency and tokens/sec.
[00:50] Priya (SecOps): A couple quick security constraints from our side: we require SOC2 Type II, SSO with SAML, audit logs to our SIEM, and KMS integration for any key material. Also data residency preference in us-east1.
[01:08] Nina (CSM): noted Priya. We'll collect exact artifact links, Maya will own SOC2 docs.
[01:16] Maya: Yep, I'll attach SOC2 and a short security questionnaire after the call.
[01:20] Elliot (PM): For success criteria: p99 inference latency under 250ms for short prompts (~64 tokens), and cost per 1k requests under our target. Also need ease of rollback during rollouts.
[01:40] Carlos: For latency we'll need to tune batching and KV cache. quick heads up, the KV cache behavior varies a bit on long contexts, might see variance up to 30% in tail latency if prefix reuse is low.
[02:05] Jenna: when you say KV cache, that's the key-value attention cache? sometimes our folks write it as K-V cache in docs.
[02:12] Carlos: yeah, K-V cache, sorry, transcription changes.
[02:18] Omar: network question: will we peer our VPC to Redwood or do you provide a private endpoint ingress?
[02:26] Maya: Both options. For Redwood Private we set up a customer-managed VPC peering or private link; for Dedicated we can offer a hosted endpoint with IP allowlist and egress controls. We'll capture the differences in the runbook.
[02:44] Priya: And encryption at rest for embeddings and logs?
[02:49] Carlos: Yes — customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM supported in Private, and we have options for encrypted-at-rest in Dedicated as well. Some terminology in our docs sometimes shows 'KMS integration' as managed keys, but we can do BYOK with the Private deployment.
[03:08] Elliot: curious about rollout tooling, canary and A/B? we want automated fallback to smaller models if the larger model blows past latency SLOs.
[03:20] Carlos: We support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. If a variant misses SLO, traffic can be rerouted to a lower-cost variant. We'll include an example policy in the runbook.
[03:40] Maya: ok, proposed 2-week runway: week 1 – staging integration + 24h throughput run; week 2 – analyze results, tune config (batching/quantization), and finalize pilot pricing. Does that align?
[03:57] Jenna: yes that seems reasonable. Who will run the 24h test?
[04:03] Carlos: I'll kick it off from our side against a staging cluster in your project or in a Redwood staging environment — depends on the network path you prefer.
[04:18] Omar: we prefer it in our GCP staging project behind our VPC to capture realistic egress.
[04:24] Carlos: good, then we'll need a short list: service account, CIDR ranges, and sample prompt set.
[04:32] Omar: I'll share the service account and a short allowlist by Wed.
[04:36] Priya: timeline for security review? we need SAML metadata exchange and a draft SLA to present to legal.
[04:44] Maya: we'll send SAML metadata sample and a standard SLA template. legal turnaround we usually see 2–3 weeks but we'll flag anything that needs faster attention.
[04:58] Jenna: what's the pilot pricing philosophy? reserved vs usage?
[05:05] Maya: two approaches — pilot on usage-based hosted API to prove metrics, then convert to Dedicated commit if you want predictable cost. For pilots we can provide a short reserved discount for the first month to reduce cost variability.
[05:22] Elliot: for our execs price visibility is key. can you provide token-level cost breakdowns in the console?
[05:29] Nina: yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost, per-route and per-model breakdowns and traces. we'll share screenshots and a short demo clip.
[05:40] Priya: any compliance attachments we should expect?
[05:44] Maya: SOC2 report, encryption docs, KMS integration doc, and a redacted runbook for the network steps.
[05:55] Carlos: technical note — if you plan heavy long-context calls, consider quantized model variants with KV chunking. reduces memory and cost but may slightly impact perplexity.
[06:10] Omar: hmm, our workload is a mix — short queries for search and some longer contextual chat sessions. we'll share usage distribution.
[06:19] Elliot: i'll prepare a histogram of token-length distribution and attach to the prompt set.
[06:24] Maya: perfect. Next up, let's walk through the staging benchmark checklist so everyone is aligned.
[06:30] Carlos: checklist items: 1) define model variant and config; 2) provide sample prompts + expected per-request token counts; 3) network setup (service account, allowlists); 4) monitoring hooks (traces, logs); 5) duration and load profile — we propose a 24h run with synthetic bursts to simulate peak and off-peak.
[06:51] Priya: can the trace logs be forwarded to our Splunk?
[06:55] Carlos: yes we support log forwarding and we can ingest traces via OTLP. there may be a small config step in your Splunk ingestion.
[07:06] Omar: what about cost attribution? we want to tag requests per-team/product so we can bill internally.
[07:13] Nina: Console supports token-level breakdown and route tagging for cost attribution. We'll show how to add metadata tags to requests.
[07:22] Jenna: ok sounds good. Any known blockers we should be aware of?
[07:28] Carlos: typical blockers are network egress rules and SSO setup. If we get those early, the bench proceeds smoothly. Also if you require air-gapped on-prem we have an extra package but it's longer to set up.
[07:44] Priya: we're not air-gapped, but legal may ask about data retention windows. we redact PII on ingest — can we enforce that before leaving our network?
[07:55] Carlos: we can do client-side redaction or use a pre-processing lambda in your VPC. We can include sample code.
[08:06] Elliot: sample prompts: we'll attach a mix that includes user queries and some system instructions. also note we prefer S3-style storage for logs.
[08:16] Maya: noted. Carlos will need the prompt set and schema.
[08:21] Carlos: another small thing — model pinning during rollouts. you can pin a version, do canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%, with auto rollback on errors or latency.
[08:33] Jenna: for our KPIs we'll want both latency and quality. can the console give quality regression alerts on prompt cohorts?
[08:40] Nina: yes, Redwood Optimize ties prompt sets to evals and can alert on quality regressions. we'll set up a baseline evaluation run post-bench.
[08:53] Priya: legal will probably ask for a data processing addendum and subprocessor list.
[08:58] Maya: we'll send a DPA template and list of subprocessors.
[09:04] Elliot: timeline recap? when will the 24h staging window start if we get the artifacts?
[09:10] Carlos: if we get service account and allowlist by Wed (2026-09-23), we can spin up the staging run the following day and finish by Fri. results and config recommendations by 2026-09-28.
[09:22] Omar: I'll try to get the network details today, but Priya needs to sign off.
[09:27] Priya: yes, i'll review tonight and aim to send allowlist by Wed.
[09:31] Maya: Great. I'll follow up with the SOC2, SAML metadata, and a short onboarding runbook draft.
[09:39] Jenna: any open questions from the SE side?
[09:42] Carlos: One thing — what model family do you want to evaluate? we can suggest a few balanced variants.
[09:48] Elliot: let's start with an efficient 7B-ish variant for the pilot and a 13B as a higher-quality comparison.
[09:54] Carlos: perfect. we'll include recommended quantization profiles and expected memory footprints.
[10:01] Maya: ok, let's close with explicit next steps and owners so nothing falls through.
[10:07] Maya: Action recap — Maya to send SOC2 + security questionnaire by 2026-09-24; Carlos to run 24h bench and share spreadsheet by 2026-09-28; Omar/Priya to provide network details by 2026-09-23; Elliot to share prompt set by 2026-09-25; Nina to schedule 30-day checkpoint for week of 2026-10-19.
[10:34] Jenna: thanks all, excited to get this moving.
[10:38] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the checkpoint and attach the docs.
[10:44] Meeting end.
